subject.title: cron.update: converting a recurring job to at skips the one-shot cleanup default

question: Does the current cron update path still preserve a recurring `deleteAfterRun: false` value when an omitted-field update converts the schedule to `at`, and should the proposed two-way transition matrix become the service contract?
rationale: The report is concrete, but protected-label handling and the unavailable local inspection prevent safely treating its source-level analysis as independently established current-main behavior.

options.title: Verify then repair
options.body: Confirm the source-level reproduction on current main and, if it holds, implement the proposed transition defaults with focused regressions for omitted and explicit values.

options.title: Retain current semantics
options.body: Keep update-time retention state unchanged across schedule-kind changes if maintainers intentionally consider it user-selected persistent state.

recommendation.title: Verify then repair
recommendation.body: Confirm the source-level reproduction on current main and, if it holds, implement the proposed transition defaults with focused regressions for omitted and explicit values.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked merged cron overhaul introduced the relevant cleanup/default and patching surfaces.
